question: I bought as a company and need our address and VAT ID on the invoices, but I already paid. Can I add it now?
reference_answer: Yes, open any invoice from Paddle and click Add address & VAT Number. Your company details and VAT number are added to invoices from then on, but invoices already issued stay as they were. With a valid VAT ID no VAT is charged on future payments, except for UK businesses, which still pay UK VAT they can reclaim.

evidence.title: View and save your invoices
evidence.text:
Our payment processor Paddle sends an invoice by email automatically after each payment. You can also view past invoices from your Plausible account. Paddle doesn't issue credit notes or receipts for refunds, so a refund has no separate document.

Log in to your Plausible account. In the top right menu, click your account name and open the settings. Scroll down in the **Subscription** section to see a list of all invoices. Select an invoice to open it in a new browser tab.

To save a PDF copy, use your browser's **Print** command and select **Save as PDF** as the destination.

Invoice list in Plausible settings

## Add your company address and VAT number

Open any invoice from Paddle and click **Add address & VAT Number**. Paddle handles VAT and sales taxes. If you provide a valid VAT ID, no VAT will be charged on future payments. UK businesses are the exception: Paddle still charges UK VAT, which you can reclaim on your VAT return. Your company details and VAT number are added to invoices from then on. Other invoices that were already issued stay as they were. When Paddle refunds the VAT on a payment after accepting your VAT number, it doesn't send a separate credit note. Instead, it reissues that payment's invoice without VAT, and the reissued invoice is the one for your records. More on Paddle's VAT handling →

## Change your billing address

Open any invoice and click **Edit business address** to update your address.

Changing the **country** on an existing subscription isn't possible due to tax regulations. To switch countries, cancel your subscription a day or two before your next renewal, then subscribe again right away from the same account with the new country (see How do I change the country on my subscription?). No data is lost in this process.

question: Can I get bounce rate for each goal in a single API query?
reference_answer: No. Mixing the session metrics bounce_rate, views_per_visit and visit_duration with event dimensions such as event:goal isn't allowed. The only exceptions are event:page, and event:hostname when it is used together with event:page.
key_facts: Session metrics can't be mixed with event dimensions
bounce_rate, views_per_visit and visit_duration are session metrics
Exceptions are event:page and event:hostname with event:page
answer: It is not possible to break down on multiple properties at the same time in a single API query [1]. If you want a breakdown by both a goal and another property, you must make multiple queries and group the results together manually or programmatically [1].

citations.quote: Currently, it is only possible to break down on one property at a time. Using a list of properties with one query is not supported.

So if you want a breakdown by both `event:page` and `visit:source` for example, you would have to make multiple queries (break down on one property and filter on another) and then manually/programmatically group the results together in one report.

evidence.title: Stats API v1 reference (legacy)
evidence.text: Currently, it is only possible to break down on one property at a time. Using a list of properties with one query is not supported. So if you want a breakdown by both `event:page` and `visit:source` for example, you would have to make multiple queries (break down on one property and filter on another) and then manually/programmatically group the results together in one report. This also applies for breaking down by time periods. To get a daily breakdown for every page, you would have to break down on `event:page` and make multiple queries for each date. For a simple time period breakdown, have a look at the Timeseries endpoint.

question: My Top Pages list shows /pricing and /pricing/ as two separate rows. How do I merge them?
reference_answer: The best fix is a 301 redirect so each page has a single address. If you can't change how your site handles URLs, you can merge them in your snippet with a `transformRequest` function that removes the trailing slash. It only affects pageviews sent after you add it, and you should update any pageview goal that ends with a slash.
key_facts: Best fix is a 301 redirect so each page has one address
Alternatively use transformRequest in the snippet to strip the trailing slash
It only changes pageviews sent after you add it
answer: If you cannot add a 301 redirect to your site to fix this duplicate content issue, you can merge these paths in your snippet [1][2]. You can use the following code to merge them: ```javascript function transformRequest(payload) { var url = new URL(payload.u) // Count /index.html as the folder it's in url.pathname = url.pathname.replace(/\/index\.html?$/, '/') // Remove the trailing slash from every path except the homepage if (url.pathname.length > 1) { url.pathname = url.pathname.replace(/\/+$/, '') } payload.u = url.toString() return payload } // At the end, update plausible.init call plausible.init({ transformRequest: transformRequest }) ``` [1]. This change only affects pageviews sent after you add it [1].

citations.quote: If you can't change how your site handles its URLs, you can merge them in your snippet instead

Plausible Analytics records the URL path of each page view as the visitors are browsing your site.

* Query parameters are discarded from the path to make sure they don't show up as different pages in Plausible. This means that pages like `yoursite.com/index.php?article=some_article&page=11` will be reported as `yoursite.com/index.php` in your Plausible dashboard. If you still want some pages to be reported with the complete URL that includes the query part, here's what you should do.

* In some cases, you might want to provide Plausible with a custom URL to use instead of the actual URL of a page. This is especially helpful to redact and aggregate multiple pages whose URLs contain user identifiers. This is helpful both from the privacy and analytics perspective. Here's how you can aggregate page URLs.

* If your website is a single-page application with `pushState` routing, Plausible Analytics will track page views automatically with no extra work. If you're using a frontend framework that uses the URL hash for routing, you can enable hash-based routing in our script.

question: i'm sending events from my backend and getting a 202 back but nothing shows up in my dashboard. what's going on?
reference_answer: The Events API returns 202 even when it drops an event, so check the response headers for x-plausible-dropped: 1, which means bot filtering rejected it. The most common cause is X-Forwarded-For containing a server or CDN IP instead of the real visitor IP. You can send a test request with the X-Debug-Request: true header to see which IP Plausible sees.
key_facts: API always returns HTTP 202 even when dropped
x-plausible-dropped: 1 header means rejected by bot filtering
Common cause is a server or CDN IP in X-Forwarded-For
X-Debug-Request: true shows the IP used
answer: The Events API returns 202 Accepted even when an event is dropped [1][2]. First, ensure you have created a matching goal in your site settings under Goals, as events are received but not displayed until the goal is created [3]. If the goal exists, your events may be rejected by bot filtering; check the response headers for x-plausible-dropped: 1 [2]. This often happens if the X-Forwarded-For header carries a server or CDN IP instead of the visitor's IP [2]. You can debug this by adding the X-Debug-Request: true header to your test requests to see the IP address Plausible uses for unique visitor counting [2].

evidence.title: Plausible Events API reference
evidence.text:
The API always returns HTTP 202 Accepted, even when an event is dropped. To debug your setup, there are two tools:

**Check if events are being dropped:** Inspect the response headers for `x-plausible-dropped: 1`. When present, the event was rejected by bot filtering. The most common cause is `X-Forwarded-For` containing a server or CDN IP instead of the actual visitor IP.

**Check which IP address Plausible sees:** Add the `X-Debug-Request: true` header to your request. The API will return HTTP 200 with the IP address it will use for unique visitor counting. Use this to confirm that `X-Forwarded-For` is being forwarded correctly from your proxy. Requests sent with this header are not recorded in your stats, so use it on separate test requests rather than on your real events.

E.g: Add this header to your request and log the response.

**Test the path your real events take.** Send an `X-Debug-Request` test request from the same place your production events are sent (your server, worker, edge function or retry job), not only from your own computer. `X-Forwarded-For` can be set correctly in your code and still reach us with a different IP: a proxy, CDN, load balancer or hosting provider along the way may replace the header or add its own address to it. If the header contains a comma-separated list, Plausible uses the first valid IP address in it, so make sure the visitor's IP comes first. Also check that the visitor's original `User-Agent` is forwarded, not your server's or HTTP library's default.

Dropped events can't be added to your stats afterwards, so it's worth running these checks whenever you set up or change your integration.
